title: billing.subscription.started payload
description: The `data` payload of the `billing.subscription.started` event: a subscription became active. A trial counts as started, which is why `status` carries the distinction rather than the type name. The payload is normalised from a payment processor's own webhook, so the ids are the processor's (`sub_…`, `cus_…`, `price_…`) and `processor`/`processor_event_id` say where the fact came from — a consumer must be able to tell a fact billing knows from a fact billing was told. There is no cafaye `plan_id` or `account_id` here, because billing has no subscriptions table and cannot invent ids it does not have: see D10. The envelope is validated by schemas/event-envelope.schema.json; this schema validates what is inside `data`. The file path is the event type with dots as directory separators. See docs/event-naming.md.

processor.description: The payment processor this subscription lives at. Present on every billing payload: an id from a processor means nothing without knowing which processor issued it, and a second processor is not a hypothetical.

processor_event_id.description: The processor's own event id for the webhook this came from, e.g. `evt_…`. The deduplication key for the ingestion, and the only way to trace a payload back to the fact it records.

kind.description: Always `subscription`. The three subscription events share one normaliser, and this is what tells a consumer which family of payload it is looking at without reading the envelope's type.

subscription_id.description: The processor's subscription id, e.g. `sub_…`. Always equal to the envelope's `subject` for this event. It is the processor's id, not a cafaye one — see D10.

customer_id.description: The processor's customer id, e.g. `cus_…`. The join back to a `billing.customer.created`, whose `processor_customer_id` is the same value. This is how a subscription event reaches an account without a subscriptions table.

status.description: The subscription's status as the processor reports it — `active`, `trialing`, `past_due`, `canceled` and whatever else it grows. Deliberately not an enum here: it is a third party's vocabulary, and core freezing it would make every processor addition a spec release. Read `trialing` for a subscription that started on a trial.

quantity.description: Units billed for, or null when the subscription carries no quantity. Seats on a per-seat plan, units on a metered one.

price_id.description: The processor's price id, e.g. `price_…`, or null. On a `billing.plan.created` payload the same value is called `processor_price_id`; the two names are the two sides' own.

unit_amount.description: Price per unit, as integer minor units and a currency — or null when the processor sent neither. Null is not zero: a missing price is missing, and defaulting it is how a customer ends up on a plan nobody charged them for.

amount_minor.description: Per-unit amount in the currency's minor units.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code, uppercase — normalised on the way in, because a processor that sends `usd` and one that sends `USD` are describing the same currency.

current_period_start.description: RFC3339 UTC when the current billing period began, or null when the processor sent no timestamp. A missing timestamp is not the epoch.

current_period_end.description: RFC3339 UTC when the current billing period ends. This is when a `cancel_at_period_end` cancellation takes effect.

cancel_at_period_end.description: Whether the subscription is set to stop at the end of the period. False is not the same as null: false is a decision, null is the absence of one.

canceled_at.description: RFC3339 UTC when the subscription was cancelled, or null while it has not been. Null on every `billing.subscription.started`.

trial.description: Whether the subscription has a trial. The boolean form of what `status: trialing` says, and unlike `status` it cannot be null — the publisher derives it.
